attempts.kind: optimized, same six as attempt 2 reordered
attempts.note: Won 12-4 with Mega Alakazam and Kartana alive. The change was not the party, it was the opening: Excadrill led beside Togekiss, Follow Me absorbed the lead pair's combination turn for two turns while Mold Breaker Earthquake hit the Levitate bodies unopposed, and I went the first four turns without losing anything. Spread damage as a rule rather than a preference is what solved the arithmetic.

protect_note: Thirteen Protects across three attempts and only one was empty (a2 T2 Camerupt). No consecutive-Protect failures anywhere in this battle, in contrast to the Alolan Graveler case at E0123. Guarding cadence here is genuinely good.

ai_observations.note: The grunt withdrew Solrock on turn one - before it had used Will-O-Wisp - and sent Hippowdon for sand. Will-O-Wisp on Solrock was precisely what beat me in attempt 1, so trading it away on turn one for weather that then chipped its own Psychic-type partner was the softest opening of the three attempts. Not a defect: switching into a Follow Me turn to deny value is defensible, and sand is a real asset. Recorded because the difference between my two losses and my win correlates exactly with whether Solrock stayed in to burn something.

Trace on my own Mega Alakazam copied Levitate (a2) and Simple (a3) off the opponents, costing it Magic Guard. In a2 that directly killed it via sandstorm chip. Worth knowing for anyone building against this battle: bringing Trace into a Sand Stream battle is a trap, and it is the opponents' typing that sets it.

level_decision: KEEP - no change to any of the twelve members. Brief rule 5 in detail: I lost two optimized attempts and won the third with 4 player faints, which is 'won after a real fight'. The reduction clause requires three lost optimized attempts and I did not reach it. More importantly, the two losses were not a level problem and I want that on the record so nobody later reads '2 losses' as a nerf trigger: attempt 1 lost to a burn I could have prevented by Fake Outing Solrock instead of Lunatone, and attempt 2 lost to a Trace/sandstorm interaction I walked into. Attempt 3 used the same six Pokemon as attempt 2 and won 12-4 by changing only the opening. That is a fight with a real solution, which is exactly what it should be. The twelve-versus-six structure makes this the hardest encounter in my block by a wide margin and it deserves to be.
cooler: This is the best-designed encounter I played in this block and I would not change a member of it. The twelve-versus-six structure does something no ordinary double can: it makes attrition the puzzle rather than a single turn, and it forces the player to actually solve the opening rather than out-stat it. The two rosters are also genuinely distinct - Courtney's is a Psychic/Rock levitating core with a Mega ace, the grunt's is a sand-and-Dark brawler pack - so it reads as two people fighting you rather than one team of twelve. Specific praise worth keeping: Solrock as a pure Helping Hand / Will-O-Wisp support with zero attacking turns is the sharpest support AI in my block, and Magcargo's Simple Shell Smash with White Herb is a real 'oh no' moment that arrives late, after the player has already spent resources. Two honest notes rather than changes. First, Minior never reached Shell Smash in three battles and never left Meteor form; it is the one member whose printed interaction stayed theoretical, and if it is meant to be the second Shell Smash threat it may want to arrive earlier than fifth. Second, the Mega Aerodactyl showcase is carried at offset -2 (L32, two levels below the player cap), which is correct for a Mega and it still took a Pokemon off me in attempt 1 - but it means the showcase dies quickly to a 2x Steel or Water move. That is a fair trade for the Mega's power and I am not proposing to change it; I am flagging that the campaign's Aerodactylite showcase is, by design, the most fragile member of the fight it appears in.
